diagram_math_checks.check: Definition lines 54–56 give q-by-q blocks of size p-by-m; both matrices therefore have qp rows and qm columns. H0 uses M_(i+j) and H1 uses M_(i+j+1); maxima are 2q-2 and 2q-1, both in the given list.

diagram_math_checks.objects_maps: R-hat: R^(qm) -> R^d; O-hat: R^d -> R^(qp)
diagram_math_checks.check: Step 2 sets the rank-d factorization with R-hat d-by-qm and O-hat qp-by-d. The top direct arrow H0 and two-edge path O-hat after R-hat agree by the explicitly verified identity H0 = O-hat R-hat.

diagram_math_checks.objects_maps: R-hat-plus: R^d -> R^(qm); H1: R^(qm) -> R^(qp); O-hat-plus: R^(qp) -> R^d
diagram_math_checks.check: A Moore–Penrose inverse reverses matrix shape. Thus the bottom path has shape (d-by-qp)(qp-by-qm)(qm-by-d) = d-by-d and agrees with the direct A-hat arrow exactly by step 4. Every arrow in both panels points left to right; matrix products act on column vectors rightmost first.

diagram_math_checks.objects_maps: B-hat: R^m -> R^d; C-hat: R^d -> R^p
diagram_math_checks.check: Step 4 takes first m columns of R-hat and first p rows of O-hat. Equivalently these restrict to the first input coordinate block and project to the first output block, respectively. This agrees with the linked experiment supplier convention M_k = CA^kB; the diagram does not shift M_k or introduce a direct-feedthrough term.
